newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank sees youth leading home buying.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank sees youth leading home buying.

text.p: Royal Bank of Canada on Thursday said its annual home buying survey found Canadians aged 18 to 34 are likely to lead the continued recovery of the residential housing market this year and next.

Canada's largest bank said about 40 percent of "Gen-Xers" said they are very or somewhat likely to be purchasing a home in the next two years, compared with 29 percent of those aged 35-54 and 13 percent for people over the age of 55.

Overall, 28 percent of those polled said they are likely to be purchasing a home in the next two years. That compared with 24 percent of adult Canadians polled last year, 20 percent in 1995 and 15 percent in 1994.

The survey found Quebec residents have the greatest desire to purchase a new home. Almost four in 10 Quebeckers say they are very or somewhat likely to purchase a home in the next two years, up from 28 percent last year, the bank said. The next most likely are B.C. residents at 27 percent, Ontario at 26 percent and Atlantic Canada at at 25 percent. Residents of the three Prairie provinces round out the list at 19 percent.
The survey also found that half of current homeowners intending to purchase a new home in the next year say they are looking for bigger, more expensive homes because they need more living space.
